words.gloss: he who possesses the nature of
he who lives in a household

literal: He who is called a householder living by the nature of virtue is he who does not desire the womanhood of her who belongs to another.
translation: He who is said to live a virtuous householder's life is one who does not lust after the womanhood of another man's wife.
modern: அறநெறியோடு இல்வாழ்க்கை வாழ்பவன் என்று சொல்லப்படுபவன், பிறனுடைய மனைவியின் பெண்மையை விரும்பாதவனே ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet defines the true standard of a virtuous householder. A person who is praised as living a righteous domestic life must possess the self-control to not covet another man's wife. The word 'piṟaṉiyalāḷ' refers to a woman who belongs to another man's household. By stating that such a householder does not desire her womanhood, the poet emphasizes that respecting the boundaries of other families is the cornerstone of domestic virtue.
